name: Hippie

influenced_by: civil rights and anti-Vietnam War activism

media.title: Joan Baez and the folk-revival scene of the early-mid 1960s

reacts_against: mainstream 1950s-60s American consumer conformity and the Vietnam War draft, building an explicitly communal, anti-materialist alternative.
revivals: a recurring festival-fashion reference ever since
article: The counterculture that became known as the hippie movement grew directly out of the Beat Generation's 1950s bohemianism, but it took shape as a distinct, much larger scene in San Francisco's Haight-Ashbury district through the mid-1960s, fed by folk music's protest tradition and a rapidly escalating opposition to the Vietnam War draft. Its look — tie-dye, fringe, flowing fabric, flowers worn in the hair — carried real political content: tie-dye and handmade clothing were partly a rejection of mass consumer culture, and long hair on men specifically coded as anti-establishment in a way that reads as merely decorative today. The movement's widest public moment came with 1967's "Summer of Love" and the 1969 Woodstock festival, both of which carried the look to a national and then international audience, after which it fragmented into later, softer commercial descendants — most directly 2000s "boho" fashion, which kept hippie's flowing silhouette and layered jewelry while leaving behind most of its original political urgency.
